newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary Westel $170 mln loan twice oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Hungary Westel $170 mln loan twice oversubscribed.

text.p: A $170 million syndicated loan for Hungarian mobile telephone network operator Westel 900 Rt has been more than twice oversubscribed, Westel 900 said in a statement on Friday.
The five-year loan, subscribed by a consortium of commercial banks organised by the U.S.'s Citibank and Bank of America, has interest of 45 basis points over LIBOR.
"No Hungarian enterprise have been able to take up a loan with such favourable conditions except (national cable telephone company) Matav," Westel said. @
Westel 900 said in October it had invested 35 billion forints in Hungary and plans to spend the same amount on development by 2000.
Westel 900 CEO Andras Sugar said that the operators of mobile telephone networks were likely to have 500,000 subscribers in Hungary by the end of this year, 700,000 in 1997 and two million by 2000.
Hungary has a population of 10.4 million.
Westel 900 is owned by, U.S. West and the International Finance Corp (IFC).
